title: Physiologically Anchored Deep Learning Using Paired Sinus Rhythm and Premature Ventricular Contraction Electrocardiograms for Ventricular Ectopic Origin Localization.
summary:
BACKGROUND: Accurate non-invasive localization of premature ventricular contractions (PVCs) is important for preprocedural planning before catheter ablation. Most artificial intelligence-based electrocardiography (ECG) models evaluate ectopic beats without incorporating patient-specific baseline ventricular conduction patterns. This study aimed to develop and evaluate a patient-referenced, QRS-centered deep learning framework integrating paired sinus rhythm and PVC 12-lead ECG recordings for binary localization of ventricular ectopic origin and to assess the incremental value of sinus rhythm information compared with PVC-only input.

METHODS: This retrospective, single-center diagnostic accuracy study included 270 patients with paired sinus rhythm and PVC ECG recordings and procedurally confirmed ventricular ectopic origin. Raw ECG signals were segmented using annotated QRS boundaries and aligned using a QRS-centered strategy. Three input strategies were evaluated: paired PVC + sinus rhythm, PVC-only, and sinus rhythm-only. A 1-dimensional residual convolutional neural network (CNN) (1D ResNet) and a 2-dimensional time-domain CNN (2D time-domain CNN) were trained directly on raw ECG waveforms, with late-fusion probability averaging used for ensemble predictions. Performance was assessed using 5-fold patient-level cross-validation. The primary endpoint was the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC).

RESULTS: For paired PVC + sinus rhythm input, pooled AUROC values were 0.753 for the 1D ResNet, 0.743 for the 2D time-domain CNN, and 0.762 for the late-fusion ensemble, with no statistically significant differences among architectures. In the cross-input comparison, ensemble AUROC was 0.762 for paired PVC + sinus rhythm, 0.731 for PVC-only, and 0.551 for sinus rhythm-only input. Paired PVC + sinus rhythm significantly outperformed PVC-only input (DeLong P = .0313), whereas sinus rhythm alone showed limited discrimination.

CONCLUSION: Patient-specific sinus rhythm information provided incremental discriminatory value when combined with PVC morphology for binary left ventricular-right ventricular (LV-RV) localization, while sinus rhythm alone had limited discriminatory value. These findings provide proof-of-concept evidence supporting paired sinus rhythm-PVC modeling as a physiologically informed approach to ventricular ectopic localization. External validation and comparison with established ECG-based localization criteria are required before clinical implementation.

title: Atrial Fibrillation and Heart Failure: One Patient, Multiple Pathways
summary: Arrhythmia & Electrophysiology Review (AER) is a tri-annual journal aimed at assisting time-pressured general and specialist cardiologists to stay abreast of key advances and opinion in the arrhythmia and electrophysiology sphere.

title: Evolving Mapping Strategies for Persistent and Long-standing Atrial Fibrillation
summary: Persistent AF remains more difficult to treat with catheter ablation than paroxysmal AF. Despite decades of evolving strategies, outcomes of durable rhythm control remain inconsistent: pulmonary vein isolation continues to be the mainstay treatment for AF, but empirical expansion of lesion sets beyond pulmonary vein isolation has not consistently improved arrhythmia-free survival in persistent AF. This review traces the evolution of AF mapping, from foundational animal studies and early human intraoperative observations to contemporary sequential and panoramic mapping platforms. Across these platforms, the central challenge has been interpretation of complex AF electrograms. Distinguishing true mechanistically relevant drivers from secondary electrical complexity has proven difficult, and randomised mapping-guided ablation trials have produced inconsistent results, with emerging artificial intelligence-assisted approaches offering a contemporary path toward reproducible, individualised substrate characterisation.

title: Pulsed Field Ablation Versus Thermal Ablation for Paroxysmal Atrial Fibrillation: A GRADE-Assessed Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials With Reconstructed Time-to-Event Analysis.
summary: Pulsed field ablation (PFA) creates myocardial lesions with brief, nonthermal electrical pulses. We synthesized randomized comparisons of PFA with radiofrequency and cryoballoon ablation for pulmonary vein isolation in paroxysmal atrial fibrillation (AF). PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library were searched from inception through October 13, 2026. We included randomized trials enrolling adults with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation and comparing PFA with thermal ablation. Random-effects models pooled risk ratios and mean differences. Leave-one-out and Baujat analyses examined sensitivity and heterogeneity. Time-to-event data were reconstructed from published Kaplan-Meier curves. Four randomized trials, reported in 6 publications, enrolled 1396 participants. For 12-month freedom from atrial arrhythmia, the 4-trial analysis (n=1392) found no significant difference (risk ratio 1.04, 95% confidence interval, 0.92-1.17; P=0.374; I2=3.6%). Reconstructed data comprised 1368 participants and 423 recurrences. Estimated 12-month freedom from recurrence was 70.6% with PFA and 66.7% with thermal ablation (log-rank p=0.097; hazard ratio 0.84, 95% confidence interval, 0.70-1.02). Procedure time was numerically lower with PFA, but the pooled result was nonsignificant and heterogeneous. Fluoroscopy time did not differ significantly; left atrial dwell time was shorter with substantial heterogeneity. No safety outcome differed significantly, and no atrioesophageal fistulas were reported. Randomized evidence indicates similar short-term efficacy for PFA and thermal ablation. The reconstructed survival analysis favored PFA numerically but did not establish a difference.

title: Marked QT Prolongation and Torsades de Pointes Following Pulsed Field Ablation for Persistent Atrial Fibrillation.
summary: Pulsed field ablation (PFA) is increasingly used for pulmonary vein isolation (PVI), but its effects on ventricular repolarization remain incompletely understood. A man in his 70s with persistent atrial fibrillation, a left ventricular ejection fraction of 18%, previous nonsustained ventricular tachycardia, and three months of amiodarone therapy underwent PVI using the FARAPULSE system (Boston Scientific Corporation, Marlborough, MA, USA). Approximately one month before PFA, automated electrocardiographic measurements showed a QT interval of 316 ms and a corrected QT interval (QTc) of 395 ms. One hour after PFA, the QT/QTc values were 356/431 ms. On postoperative day one, the QT/QTc values increased to 602/610 ms, accompanied by frequent premature ventricular contractions and a serum potassium concentration of 3.2 mEq/L. On postoperative day two, telemetry demonstrated a short-long-short sequence immediately before torsades de pointes, which was initiated by a premature ventricular contraction when the QT/QTc values were 490/510 ms and serum potassium was 3.0 mEq/L. Altered consciousness developed, and one 150-J direct-current shock terminated the arrhythmia. After potassium and magnesium replacement, no recurrence occurred. The QTc decreased to 479 ms on postoperative day four and 403 ms at one month. The event was probably multifactorial; severe ventricular dysfunction, residual amiodarone effects, hypokalemia, and transient postprocedural hypoxemia prevent attribution of causality to PFA alone. Nevertheless, the marked but reversible QT prolongation after the procedure supports careful monitoring of the QT interval, ventricular ectopy, and electrolytes after PFA in susceptible patients.

title: Elevated pericoronary adipose tissue attenuation assessed by fat attenuation index in atrial fibrillation without cardiovascular comorbidities: a retrospective observational study.
summary:
BACKGROUND: Atrial fibrillation (AF) without cardiovascular comorbidities is a distinct entity with poorly understood pathophysiology. Inflammation contributes to AF, but pericoronary adipose tissue has not been characterized in this population. We examined the association between pericoronary adipose tissue attenuation, assessed by the fat attenuation index (FAI), an imaging surrogate of inflammation-related adipose tissue remodeling rather than a direct measure of inflammation, and AF without cardiovascular comorbidities.

METHODS: This retrospective, exploratory study included 125 patients undergoing coronary CT angiography (CCTA) for chest pain at two tertiary hospitals: 30 with AF without cardiovascular comorbidities (REGARDS criteria; CAD-RADS 0 coronary arteries) and 95 non-AF controls. Pericoronary FAI and fat volume were measured for the three coronary arteries (LAD, LCX, RCA). Systemic inflammatory ratios (NLR, LMR, PLR) were compared, and logistic regression identified independent predictors.

RESULTS: FAI was significantly higher in all three coronary arteries, most markedly the RCA (-79.90 ± 7.04 vs. -89.73 ± 10.43 HU, p < 0.001; LAD and LCX both p ≤ 0.008). Although the LMR was lower in the AF group, no FAI measurement correlated with the systemic inflammatory ratios. In multivariable analysis adjusted for age and sex, RCA-FAI (OR 1.11, p < 0.001) and RCA volume (OR 2.38 per SD, p = 0.003) were independent predictors of AF without cardiovascular comorbidities.

CONCLUSIONS: AF without cardiovascular comorbidities is associated with elevated pericoronary FAI that was not explained by routine circulating leukocyte ratios. Given the sample size and the absence of tissue or cytokine confirmation, these findings are hypothesis-generating and require validation in larger prospective cohorts.

title: Electrothermal multiphysics coupling mechanisms and experimental study on the effect of left atrial appendage occluders on the efficacy of pulsed field ablation.
summary:
BACKGROUND: Pulsed field ablation (PFA) is a novel non-thermal technique, but its effect on tissues with left atrial appendage occluders (LAAOs) has not been fully and effectively evaluated. Objective: This comprehensive study systematically analyzes the influence of LAAOs on ablation zones and temperature rise via multiphysics coupled computational simulations and ex vivo tissue experiments.

METHODS: A simplified target model was developed. Lesion extent was assessed using the 400 V/cm isoelectric contour, while temperature changes in the ablation zone were recorded simultaneously. Animal myocardial tissue was used for validation purposes.

RESULTS: Electrode configuration significantly affected ablation outcomes. Configuration 2 exacerbated electric field distortion, causing incomplete lesion formation. The maximum temperature difference across configurations was 2.61°C, with a peak of 45.45°C. The spatial relationship between electrode and LAAO also quantitatively influenced the ablation zone. Ex vivo experiments showed negligible field distortion, uniform lesion width and depth, and progressive temperature rise with pulse parameters.

CONCLUSION: LAAO minimally impacts the target zone. Different electrode configurations adjust the ablation range without causing thermal injury. Ex vivo data confirmed the temperature rise effect. This study offers important clinical guidance for circular catheter PFA treatment in atrial fibrillation patients with an LAAO.

title: Atrial Fibrillation, Atrial Flutter, and Orthodromic Atrioventricular Re-Entrant Tachycardia With a Concealed Left-Sided Accessory Pathway.
summary:
BACKGROUND: Accessory pathway (AP)-mediated tachycardias are a common cause of supraventricular tachycardia; however, their relationship with atrial fibrillation (AF) and atrial flutter (AFL) is often under-recognized.

CASE SUMMARY: A 61-year-old man presented with recurrent narrow-complex tachycardia, AF, and typical AFL occurring in close temporal proximity. An electrophysiology study demonstrated inducible orthodromic atrioventricular re-entrant tachycardia with eccentric retrograde atrial activation, consistent with a concealed left inferoposterior AP. The pathway was successfully ablated. At 9-month follow-up, there was no recurrence of AF, AFL, or supraventricular tachycardia.

DISCUSSION: Prior studies suggest APs may facilitate atrial arrhythmogenesis. This case highlights the interplay between atrioventricular re-entrant tachycardia and atrial arrhythmias and the importance of recognizing multiple mechanisms in a single patient.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGES: Concealed APs may trigger AF and AFL. Targeted ablation can eliminate multiple arrhythmias.

title: [Berberine targets Smurf2 to regulate the TGF-β/Smads signaling pathway and alleviate myocardial fibrosis in rats with atrial fibrillation]
summary: Berberine may alleviate myocardial fibrosis in atrial fibrillation rats by targeting Smurf2 to inhibit the TGF-β/Smads signaling pathway.

title: [Risk factors for long-term new-onset atrial fibrillation after percutaneous intramyocardial septal radiofrequency ablation in patients with hypertrophic obstructive cardiomyopathy]
summary: Baseline LAD is an independent influencing factor for long-term new-onset AF after PIMSRA in HOCM patients. It can assist clinicians in early identification of high-risk individuals and formulation of individualized follow-up strategies.

title: [Advances in pulsed field ablation for ventricular arrhythmias]
AIM-AF score: R code for the development and temporal validation of a bedside score to predict atrial fibrillation after isolated coronary artery bypass grafting
summary: R code for the development and temporal validation of the AIM-AF score (age, left ventricular ejection fraction and estimated glomerular filtration rate) to predict new-onset postoperative atrial fibrillation after isolated on-pump coronary artery bypass grafting, as reported in: Grassi NC, et al. A Simple Bedside Score to Predict Atrial Fibrillation After Isolated Coronary Artery Bypass Grafting: Development and Temporal Validation of the AIM-AF Score (submitted to Heart, Lung and Circulation). The pipeline covers cohort selection, model fitting and point derivation, bootstrap optimism correction, calibration, temporal validation (2017–2022 to 2023–2026), comparison with the POAF score, POLARIS and ACEF, categorical net reclassification, decision curve analysis, sensitivity and subgroup analyses, and a supporting analysis with prespecified candidate predictors (full model and LASSO). It generates the manuscript tables, figures and the key-number file. No patient-level data are included. Anonymized individual data may be made available upon reasonable request to the corresponding author, subject to approval by the Research Ethics Committee and in accordance with the Brazilian General Data Protection Law (LGPD; Law 13.709/2018).
journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

title: Apical hypertrophic cardiomyopathy complicated by multisystem embolism, anticoagulant overdose-induced iliopsoas hematoma, and subsequent cardiocerebral infarction: a cautionary case report on DOAC dosing in renal impairment.
summary:
BACKGROUND: Apical hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (ApHCM) is a morphological variant of hypertrophic cardiomyopathy characterized by relative apical hypertrophy (wall thickness ≥ 15 mm) with a relatively favourable prognosis. Approximately 30% of patients with ApHCM develop one or more adverse cardiovascular complications, among which atrial fibrillation (AF) is the most prevalent, with a reported incidence of 12%. Atrial fibrillation (AF) is a common cardiac arrhythmia and a major risk factor for stroke and systemic thromboembolism.

CASE PRESENTATION: A 78-year-old man complained of a 1-day history of severe, lower abdominal pain associated with nausea and hematuria. Simultaneous renal infarctions and splenic infarctions were then diagnosed. The patient was initiated on subcutaneous enoxaparin sodium injection 4000 anti-Xa IU /12 h, and his abdominal pain improved after six days of anticoagulation. Anticoagulation therapy was transitioned to oral edoxaban 60 mg once daily after discharge. Five days later, the man was admitted to our emergency room again with complaints of progressively increasing right lower quadrant abdominal pain and a large palpable abdominal mass. Pelvic magnetic resonance imaging revealed an oval, irregular heterogeneous signal lesion measuring 7.9 × 5.8 cm adjacent to the right iliopsoas muscle, consistent with a hematoma.

CONCLUSIONS: In patients with acute renal infarctions and secondary upward-trending creatinine, the treatment decisions regarding anticoagulants are of crucial importance as the worsening kidney function can considerably increase the incidence of embolism and bleeding. For this patient with progressively elevated serum creatinine and a creatinine clearance of 39.7 mL/min, the administration of edoxaban 60 mg once daily was an iatrogenic dosing error. This guideline-noncompliant full dose resulted in a rare iliopsoas hematoma. According to clinical guidelines, edoxaban is indicated for stroke prophylaxis in patients with atrial fibrillation. For those with creatinine clearance (CrCl) ranging from 15 to 50 mL/min, the standard reduced dose is 30 mg once daily.

title: AI-Assisted Multimodal Imaging Integration for Individualized Transseptal Puncture Planning During Atrial Fibrillation Ablation.
summary: Transseptal puncture (TSP) is a critical step during atrial fibrillation (AF) ablation, and accurate anatomical understanding of the interatrial septum is essential for individualized procedural planning. Intracardiac echocardiography (ICE) provides real-time visualization of septal anatomy but is limited by its two-dimensional representation and operator dependence. This study developed an artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted multimodal imaging framework integrating preprocedural computed tomography angiography (CTA) with intraoperative ICE to provide patient-specific three-dimensional (3D) anatomical guidance for TSP planning. This single-center study enrolled 700 patients undergoing AF ablation. An AI framework was developed using data from 500 patients to perform automated segmentation, 3D reconstruction, and CTA-ICE multimodal image integration. The framework was evaluated in an independent temporal validation cohort of 200 patients. The primary outcome was the influence of AI-assisted anatomical information on individualized TSP planning, assessed by changes in puncture strategy following AI-assisted assessment. Secondary outcomes included decision confidence, planning time, interreader agreement, and procedural feasibility. The AI framework achieved an overall Dice similarity coefficient of 0.854 for automated anatomical segmentation and a Dice coefficient of 0.862 for 3D left atrial reconstruction. In the temporal validation cohort, at least one AI-recommended adjustment was incorporated into the final TSP strategy in 68 patients (34.0%). The recommendations addressed involved three key components of TSP planning: puncture site category in 52 patients (26.0%), puncture direction in 61 patients (30.5%), and puncture trajectory or angle in 74 patients (37.0%). AI-assisted assessment increased decision confidence (4.3 ± 0.6 vs. 3.4 ± 0.8, p < 0.001), reduced planning time (28.7 ± 10.3 vs. 42.5 ± 15.2 s, p < 0.001), and improved interreader agreement for anatomical assessment. In the temporal validation cohort, acute successful TSP was achieved in 196 patients (98.0%), with a mean transseptal time of 6.8-2.5 min and an overall complication rate of 3.0%. AI-assisted integration of preprocedural CTA with intraoperative ICE provides patient-specific 3D anatomical information that supports individualized TSP planning. The proposed framework demonstrated feasibility and compatibility with anatomical assessment and procedural planning, hopefully contributing to improve procedural or clinical outcomes.

title: Electrical storm due to ectopic activity following successful reperfusion: Clinical characterization and pharmacological approach to angry Purkinje syndrome
summary: Introduction: Angry Purkinje syndrome is an uncommon cause of electrical storm characterized by short-coupled premature ventricular complexes (PVCs) originating from the His-Purkinje system and triggering polymorphic ventricular tachycardia (PMVT) or ventricular fibrillation (VF). It may occur during the subacute phase after myocardial infarction despite successful coronary reperfusion and absence of recurrent ischemia. Case presentation: A 55-year-old man presented with persistent oppressive precordial chest pain, rated 8/10, radiating to the jaw and left arm, which had begun at 02:00 h while asleep, without associated autonomic symptoms. On admission, blood pressure was 174/101 mmHg and heart rate was 103 beats/min. Electrocardiography showed an extensive anterior myocardial infarction, and primary percutaneous coronary intervention restored TIMI 3 flow in the left anterior descending coronary artery. Seventy-two hours after complete coronary revascularization, the patient developed ventricular fibrillation requiring external defibrillation with 150 J (Figure 2E). At the time of the first arrest, serum troponin was 896 pg/mL, potassium was 4.5 mEq/L, and magnesium was 2.62 mEq/L. The heart rate was 50 beats/min, with a QTc of 413 ms. Continuous cardiac monitoring subsequently demonstrated frequent premature ventricular complexes (PVCs) with a coupling interval of approximately 380 ms and a right bundle branch block morphology with a superior axis, followed by episodes of polymorphic ventricular tachycardia (PMVT) initiated by short-coupled PVCs (Figure 2A–D). Following this event, diagnostic coronary angiography was performed because of suspected acute stent thrombosis, confirming patency of the left anterior descending coronary artery stent with TIMI 3 flow and no new angiographic lesions in the remaining coronary arteries. Conclusion: Angry Purkinje syndrome should be considered in patients who develop recurrent PMVT or VF initiated by short-coupled PVCs after successful myocardial reperfusion, particularly when recurrent ischemia has been excluded. Flecainide combined with atrial overdrive pacing may represent a potential rescue strategy when quinidine is unavailable; however, further evidence is required to determine its efficacy and safety in this setting.

title: Sudden Cardiac Arrest As the Initial Presentation of Anomalous Left Coronary Artery Originating From the Pulmonary Artery in a Young Adult: A Case Report.
summary: Anomalous left coronary artery from the pulmonary artery (ALCAPA) is a rare congenital heart condition associated with high childhood mortality if untreated. Consequently, diagnosis in asymptomatic adults is exceedingly uncommon. We report a 21-year-old gentleman brought to hospital via the primary percutaneous coronary intervention service after an out-of-hospital ventricular fibrillation arrest while hiking. Following prehospital cardiopulmonary resuscitation and defibrillation, return of spontaneous circulation was achieved; an immediate 12-lead electrocardiogram showed ST elevation. Initial transthoracic echocardiography revealed abnormal myocardial color Doppler flow, suggesting intercoronary collaterals and raising suspicion of a coronary anomaly. Coronary angiography confirmed ALCAPA. He underwent successful reimplantation surgery. Given myocardial fibrosis on cardiac magnetic resonance imaging, a subcutaneous implantable cardioverter-defibrillator was implanted for secondary prevention. Sudden cardiac arrest as the initial presenting symptom is exceedingly rare in an asymptomatic young adult with ALCAPA. High clinical suspicion supports early diagnosis. Multi-modality imaging remains central to diagnosis and device-therapy decisions after corrective surgery.

title: Long QT syndrome presenting as convulsions in a preeclamptic patient: a case report.
summary:
BACKGROUND: Eclampsia is the leading cause of convulsions in patients with preeclampsia. To the best of our knowledge, convulsions secondary to long QT syndrome (LQTS) in the setting of preeclampsia have been reported only rarely. The overlapping clinical manifestations of these two conditions make differential diagnosis challenging. Delayed recognition and inadequate management may place patients at high risk of sudden cardiac death.

CASE PRESENTATION: A 31-year-old pregnant woman at 35 + 4 weeks of gestation was initially diagnosed with acute heart failure complicated by preeclampsia and transferred to our institution after initial intensive therapy. After her cardiac function stabilized, a cesarean section was scheduled. Immediately after being positioned, the patient developed sudden syncope and convulsions, which were initially misdiagnosed as eclampsia. Recurrent syncope and persistent convulsions occurred on the second day postpartum. Electrocardiogram monitoring detected torsade de pointes that rapidly deteriorated into ventricular fibrillation. Emergency electrical defibrillation and cardiopulmonary resuscitation were performed, and sinus rhythm was successfully restored. The patient subsequently developed respiratory depression and received endotracheal intubation and mechanical ventilation. A repeat electrocardiogram showed significant prolongation of the corrected QT interval. The patient was extubated the next day with no recurrent convulsive episodes. Retrospective analysis of cardiac recordings captured during the initial convulsive episode revealed non-sustained ventricular tachycardia (NSVT) that spontaneously reverted to sinus rhythm within seconds. Ultimately, the patient's convulsions were attributed to malignant arrhythmias triggered by a prolonged QTc interval in the context of preeclampsia.

CONCLUSION: Preeclampsia combined with LQTS is a rare and life-threatening, yet preventable, clinical entity. It is frequently misdiagnosed as eclampsia, which often leads to improper management. Clinicians should maintain high vigilance for this comorbidity, achieve early identification, and initiate prompt intervention to prevent sudden cardiac death.

title: Intraoperative rescue left stellate ganglion block for refractory ventricular arrhythmias following resuscitation from torsades de pointes: a case report.
summary:
BACKGROUND: Congenital long QT syndrome (cLQTS) predisposes patients to torsades de pointes (TdP) under sympathetic stress. Although ultrasound-guided left stellate ganglion block (LSGB) can rapidly achieve cardiac sympathetic blockade, its application in intraoperative rescue has been scarcely documented.

CASE: A 53-year-old woman with clinically suspected cLQTS (QTc 499 ms) developed pulseless TdP during fracture manipulation under general anesthesia. Following restoration of spontaneous circulation, frequent ventricular ectopy and short runs of TdP persisted despite treatment with magnesium sulfate, lidocaine, and esmolol. Following concomitant multimodal antiarrhythmic therapy, LSGB was performed with 5 mL of 0.25% ropivacaine, and a marked reduction of arrhythmias was observed shortly afterwards. No recurrent ventricular arrhythmias were observed during subsequent treatment and follow-up.

CONCLUSIONS: LSGB may be considered as an adjunct to pharmacological therapy when ventricular arrhythmia responds suboptimally and is presumed to be exacerbated by sympathetic stimulation in patients with QT prolongation.

title: Temporal sequence of changes of monophasic action potentials preceding ventricular fibrillation after acute myocardial infarction in a pig model: Mechanistic insights.
summary: Ventricular fibrillation (VF) is the most common arrhythmia leading to cardiac arrest after acute myocardial infarction (AMI). This study aimed to investigate alterations in ischemia-induced action potentials that preceded the onset of VF. AMI was induced by ligation of the left anterior descending (LAD) coronary artery in 11 anesthetized open-chest pigs. Monophasic action potentials (MAPs) were recorded from the left ventricular endocardium using combination FRANZ® MAP-Stimulation catheters. Epicardial MAPs recordings were obtained using specially designed probes. Changes in MAPs morphology and surface ECG were monitored at 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, and 20 min following the onset of ischemia. Among animals studied, 9 out of 11 developed spontaneous VF and exhibited either type I early afterdepolarizations (EADs I, 6/9) or type II (EADs II, 3/9) in ischemia-affected MAPs. The earliest electrophysiological changes included acceleration of phase-1 of MAP and appearance of peaked T waves on the ECG. EADs I appeared at 4.7 ± 1.5 min after LAD ligation whereas EADs II appeared later, at 10 ± 3.5 min, both occurring concurrently with ST-segment elevation. Animals exhibiting EADs I developed very early 2:1 plateau alternans and frequent R-on-T extrasystoles. In contrast, EADs II animals displayed MAP duration alternans. Alternans consistently preceded VF, which was typically initiated after a prolonged pause between two consecutive R-on-T events. The remaining two animals that did not develop VF exhibited only low-amplitude EADs II and showed neither alternans nor R-on-T phenomenon during the first 10 min of ischemia. We conclude that EADs I were the most prevalent and earliest MAP alteration observed after AMI and were followed by plateau alternans and R-on-T phenomena, potentially predisposing to VF. These findings imply that EADs I may constitute a key electrophysiological mechanism underlying sudden cardiac arrest during the early stage of infarction.

title: [Electrocardiographic and intracardiac bipolar electrogram characteristics of ventricular arrhythmias originating from the right coronary cusp]
summary: RCC-VAs are relatively uncommon, but their ECG and intracardiac bipolar electrogram features differ clearly from LCC-and RVOT-VAs. The transition index, lead Ⅰ morphology, and lead V₁ morphology can be used to distinguish LVOT from RVOT origin and to localize wall versus bottom origin within the RCC.

title: Cutaneous warning signs of cardiac implantable electronic device infection: a pictorial guide for clinicians.
summary: Cardiac implantable electronic device (CIED) infections are potentially life-threatening complications of pacemakers, implantable cardioverter-defibrillators, and cardiac resynchronization therapy devices. Although fever, bacteremia, and infective endocarditis may occur, the earliest-and sometimes only-manifestations are cutaneous abnormalities overlying the generator pocket. These findings may be subtle and mistaken for postoperative changes, hematoma, contact dermatitis, mechanical irritation, or impaired wound healing. Because patients may initially present to general practitioners, internists, emergency physicians, or dermatologists, early recognition is essential. This pictorial review illustrates the spectrum of cutaneous manifestations of CIED infection, ranging from localized erythema, swelling, pain, and delayed wound healing to erosion, sinus tract formation, purulent drainage, necrosis, and hardware exposure. It also highlights practical warning signs, appropriate referral pathways, and interventions that should be avoided before specialist assessment. Infection may extend from the pocket along the intravascular leads to the bloodstream and cardiac structures, leading to bacteremia, endocarditis, sepsis, and death. Any persistent or progressive abnormality over a CIED pocket warrants prompt evaluation, whereas purulent drainage, sinus formation, or hardware exposure should be considered evidence of device infection and require urgent electrophysiology assessment, even in the absence of systemic symptoms.

title: Dual-Chamber Leadless Pacemaker Implantation in Dextrocardia With Situs Inversus.
summary:
BACKGROUND: Dextrocardia with situs inversus presents unique anatomical challenges for cardiac device implantation. AVEIR DR dual-chamber leadless pacemaker system implantation has not previously been reported in this setting.

CASE SUMMARY: An 84-year-old man with dextrocardia and situs inversus underwent AVEIR DR dual-chamber leadless pacemaker system implantation for symptomatic bradycardia. Preprocedural 3-dimensional computed tomography merged with intraprocedural fluoroscopy, together with right atrial contrast angiography and fluoroscopic guidance, facilitated successful implantation of both devices. The procedure was completed without complications, and the subsequent clinical course was uneventful.

DISCUSSION: To the best of our knowledge, this is the first reported experience of AVEIR DR dual-chamber leadless pacemaker system implantation in a patient with dextrocardia and situs inversus totalis.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: Careful preprocedural anatomical planning, catheter manipulation adapted to mirror-image anatomy, and a systematic implantation strategy enabled successful dual-chamber leadless pacemaker implantation in a patient with dextrocardia and situs inversus.

title: Conduction System Pacing With DF-1 ICD Systems Using a Medtronic 3830 Lead: A Feasibility Study.
summary:
BACKGROUND: Patients with implantable cardioverter-defibrillators (ICDs) who require ventricular pacing are at risk for pacing-induced cardiomyopathy (PICM) from chronic right ventricular (RV) pacing. Conduction system pacing (CSP), particularly left bundle branch area pacing (LBBAP), offers more physiologic ventricular activation, but integration with ICD therapy remains challenging. The DF-1 ICD connector standard provides an opportunity to incorporate a separate CSP lead while maintaining high-voltage ICD therapy. We evaluated the feasibility of an alternative ICD configuration using a DF-1 defibrillation lead paired with a Medtronic 3830 CSP lead connected to a dual-chamber ICD generator.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective case series of 17 consecutive patients who underwent this configuration at a single center between October 2022 and August 2025. For subgroup analyses, patients were stratified by baseline left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) as LVEF ≤ 50% (n = 9) or LVEF > 50% (n = 8). QRS duration, LVEF, left ventricular end-systolic dimension (LVESD), tricuspid regurgitation (TR) severity, and device outcomes were assessed during follow-up.

RESULTS: Median follow-up was 15.0 months (IQR 6.2-19.2). The Medtronic 3830 lead was successfully implanted in all 17 patients, with confirmed LBBAP in 16 patients (94.1%) and deep septal pacing without definitive left bundle branch capture in one patient. No CSP lead revisions for mechanical or electrical failure were required. Among patients with paired measurements, LVEF increased from 41.6% ± 15.0% to 45.9% ± 14.1%, although the change was not statistically significant (p = 0.169), while LVESD decreased from 4.33 ± 0.72 cm to 3.89 ± 0.79 cm (p = 0.022). In paired subgroup analyses, patients with baseline LVEF ≤50% demonstrated an increase in LVEF from 31.9% ± 6.2% to 40.1% ± 14.3% (p = 0.053) and a decrease in LVESD from 4.62 ± 0.65 cm to 4.11 ± 0.71 cm (p = 0.048), whereas patients with baseline LVEF >50% demonstrated no significant change in either measure. QRS duration did not change significantly in either subgroup. Overall TR severity did not change significantly (Bhapkar p = 0.337), although 5 of 12 patients with paired imaging experienced at least a one-grade increase in TR severity and no patient developed new severe TR. Two patients (11.8%) died during follow-up, with neither death attributed to the device configuration.

CONCLUSION: An ICD configuration using a DF-1 defibrillation lead paired with a Medtronic 3830 CSP lead on a dual-chamber generator was technically feasible, with successful 3830 lead implantation in all patients, confirmed LBBAP in 94.1%, and no CSP lead revisions for mechanical or electrical failure during intermediate-term follow-up. Patients with baseline LVEF ≤50% demonstrated numerical improvement in LVEF and a reduction in LVESD, while ventricular function remained stable in those with LVEF >50%. These exploratory findings require confirmation in larger prospective comparative studies.

title: Two Is Not too Small; a Case of a Ventricular Aveir AR2 for Ventricular Pacing in a 12.2-kg Two-Year-Old.
summary: Pacemaker implants in pediatric patients can be filled with potential complications. Epicardial pacemaker implants are the usual mainstay for those under 15 kg and transvenous devices can have infectious and pocket erosion risk. Retrievable leadless pacemakers seem to be a potential option. Retrospective review of a 2-year-old patient with high grade AV block and overall lowering average junctional rate was performed. Internal review board approval was obtained. A 2-year-old, 12.2-kg female underwent successful right internal jugular vein implant of an Aveir AR2 into the right ventricle for backup ventricular pacing need. No complications occurred. Follow-up at 12 months demonstrated a threshold of 0.5 Volts @0.2 ms, impedance at 420 ohms and sensing at 10milliVolts with 30% pacing noted with programming at VVI 50 bpm, with predicted longevity at 20.2 years. Feasibility of internal jugular vein implant of an Aveir AR2 is possible without complication in a 2-year-old, 12.2 kg child. Further prospective studies are needed to assess true feasibility in this population.

title: Transthyretin cardiac amyloidosis: an evolving paradigm in recognition, diagnosis, and treatment.
summary: Transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy (ATTR-CM) has evolved from an underrecognized and largely untreatable infiltrative cardiomyopathy into a paradigm of precision cardiovascular medicine. The disease arises from transthyretin tetramer destabilization, protein misfolding, and progressive extracellular amyloid deposition, processes that ultimately shape its multisystem clinical phenotype. Importantly, the biology of ATTR-CM is often clinically apparent years before overt heart failure through extracardiac manifestations, including carpal tunnel syndrome, spinal stenosis, and tendon disease,. Recognition of this disease continuum has transformed diagnostic strategies, with contemporary evaluation integrating clinical red flags, multimodality imaging, exclusion of light-chain amyloidosis, radionuclide imaging, and genetic testing to establish ATTR subtype. Emerging artificial intelligence-enabled electrocardiographic and imaging approaches may further shift recognition toward earlier, pre-diagnostic disease recognition, although their clinical utility requires prospective validation. Management has undergone an equally profound transformation. Beyond physiology-guided treatment of heart failure, atrial fibrillation, and thromboembolic risk, disease-modifying therapies now directly target the amyloidogenic cascade through stabilization of circulating transthyretin or suppression of its hepatic synthesis. Cardiovascular outcome evidence for TTR silencers is currently agent-specific: vutrisiran demonstrated clinical benefit in HELIOS-B, whereas eplontersen did not significantly reduce the primary cardiovascular endpoint in CARDIO-TTRansform. The therapeutic frontier is expanding further toward monoclonal antibodies designed to promote clearance of established amyloid deposits, raising the possibility of moving from disease stabilization toward myocardial amyloid regression. This review integrates the molecular pathogenesis, clinical and imaging phenotype, contemporary diagnostic framework, emerging role of artificial intelligence, and rapidly evolving therapeutic landscape of ATTR-CM.

title: Case Report: Suspected biventricular arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy presenting as a dilated cardiomyopathy-like phenotype with multimodal phenotyping and cautious genetic interpretation.
summary: Arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy (ACM) may overlap clinically with dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM), particularly when left ventricular dilatation and systolic dysfunction dominate the presentation. We report a 47-year-old man initially diagnosed with DCM whose subsequent multimodal assessment suggested a biventricular ACM (BiV-ACM) phenotype. The clinical assessment integrated clinical history, electrocardiography, ambulatory rhythm monitoring, echocardiography, and cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) imaging. Findings included marked left ventricular dilatation, severe systolic dysfunction, frequent multifocal ventricular ectopy, nonsustained ventricular tachycardia, right ventricular dysfunction, and biventricular nonischemic myocardial abnormalities on CMR. These phenotypic findings, rather than genetic results, formed the basis of the clinical impression. Whole-exome sequencing performed during follow-up identified four heterozygous variants of uncertain significance, including the truncating DSP variant NM_004415.4:c.7423A>T [p.(Lys2475Ter)]. None provided molecular confirmation. Over approximately 2 years of medical treatment and follow-up, left ventricular ejection fraction increased from 28.9% to 35%, and peak oxygen uptake increased from 24.4 to 26.7 mL/kg/min, while ventricular arrhythmias persisted. These observations do not establish an intervention-specific treatment effect. This case highlights the value of phenotype-based multimodal assessment in DCM-like presentations and the importance of distinguishing uncertain genetic findings from diagnostic evidence.

title: Myeloid-fibroblast-cardiomyocyte crosstalk in atrial fibrillation: hypertension and evidence across disease models.
summary: Hypertension is a major antecedent of atrial fibrillation, but pressure load alone does not explain the development of an arrhythmogenic atrial substrate. Wall stress and neurohumoral activation can recruit circulating myeloid cells, alter macrophage states, activate fibroblasts, and disrupt cardiomyocyte inflammatory signaling and calcium handling. This review examines evidence from hypertensive animals, mixed-risk-factor models, human atrial tissue, and non-hypertensive models, separating findings demonstrated in each setting from their proposed relevance to hypertension. Macrophage osteopontin promotes fibroblast matrix programs in mixed-risk-factor models. Fibroblast-restricted NOD-like receptor family pyrin domain containing 3 (NLRP3) inflammasome activation promotes fibrosis and conduction abnormalities in a non-hypertensive model. Separate experiments link cardiomyocyte NLRP3 or N-terminal gasdermin D signaling to inflammatory output and arrhythmogenic remodeling. These mechanisms may converge, but neither a serial osteopontin-fibroblast NLRP3 pathway nor a complete three-cell causal circuit has been established in hypertension. Blood-pressure-matched experiments, spatially resolved human atrial studies, and interventions that distinguish recruited pathological states from resident reparative macrophages are needed to test these links. Such studies may identify the disease stages and cell states in which immune modulation can complement control of hemodynamic stress.

title: MKP-ECG: A Knowledge-Enhanced Dual-Stream Network for Robust Arrhythmia Classification with Medical Prior-Guided Multi-Loss Optimization.
summary: Accurate classification of cardiac arrhythmias from electrocardiogram (ECG) signals is essential for clinical decision-making, yet deep learning models often struggle with minority classes such as Fusion beats (F-type) owing to severe class imbalance and insufficient integration of domain knowledge. In this work, we propose Medical Knowledge Prior Network (MKP-ECG), a knowledge-enhanced dual-stream network for four-class arrhythmia classification (N, S, V, F) following the AAMI standard. The first stream employs a multi-scale CNN with residual connections and squeeze-and-excitation attention to learn data-driven representations from raw waveforms. The second stream, termed the Medical Prior Module, extracts a 34-dimensional clinical feature vector encoding morphology, rhythm, template matching, and rule-based indicators that mirror the reasoning process of cardiologists. The two streams are fused through explicit feature concatenation and a knowledge attention gate that dynamically modulates neural representations based on clinical evidence, and are jointly optimized by a composite loss function comprising two novel medical knowledge prior losses: a knowledge graph KL-divergence loss that aligns predictions with expert-defined electrophysiological priors and a clinical constraint loss that penalizes predictions contradicting established diagnostic criteria. Evaluated on the MIT-BIH Arrhythmia Database under the inter-patient DS1/DS2 paradigm with methodologically corrected data augmentation (waveform-only SMOTE with nearest-neighbor clinical feature copying and purity-weighted contrastive loss), MKP-ECG achieves 99.14% accuracy, 92.77% Macro-F1, and 76.98% F-class F1-score with perfect F-recall, representing a 51.7% relative improvement over the knowledge-free baseline. Independent evaluation on the INCART database, where the model is trained and tested entirely within INCART using the same architecture and hyperparameters without any dataset-specific tuning, provides encouraging evidence of architectural generalizability under a record-split protocol, achieving 99.71% accuracy and 87.43% F-class F1-score.

title: Clinically significant hypokalaemia and the utilisation of cardiac telemetry in hospitalised adults.
summary:
AIM: Hypokalaemia is one of the most common electrolyte abnormalities in hospitalised patients, with moderate (2.5-3.0 mmol/L) to severe (< 2.5 mmol/L) deficiency associated with an increased risk of cardiac arrhythmias, prolonged hospitalisation, and inpatient mortality [1]. While clinical guidelines recommend the use of continuous cardiac monitoring (telemetry) for patients with moderate to severe hypokalaemia, there is limited evidence of adherence to these recommendations, and a lack of understanding of the resultant patient outcomes. This study aimed to characterise the clinical features, pattern of telemetry utilisation, and outcomes of adults admitted with clinically significant hypokalaemia at a major Australian tertiary hospital.

METHODS: A retrospective cohort study was conducted at Townsville University Hospital (TUH) between January 2017 and August 2023. Adult inpatients (≥ 18 years) with an initial serum potassium concentration ≤ 3.0 mmol/L were included. Data was extracted from electronic medical records, including demographics, comorbidities, inpatient telemetry use, and hospitalisation outcomes. The primary outcome was telemetry utilisation, with secondary outcomes including time to normalisation of serum potassium concentration, length of stay (LOS), ICU transfer, and inpatient mortality. Statistical analysis included Chi-square tests, logistic regression, log-rank testing, and survival analysis.

RESULTS: A total of 5,035 unique patients with a total of 11,143 admissions (1.6% of total admissions) were included, with a mean age of 64.0 years and a median admission potassium of 2.9 mmol/L. Cardiac telemetry was utilised in 3.7% of patients. Cox regression demonstrated that telemetry use was more likely amongst patients with higher Charlson Comorbidity Index (CCI) scores (p < 0.001) and prior arrhythmia diagnosis (p = 0.028), but its use was not significantly associated with hypokalaemia severity. Telemetry use was independently associated with longer hospital stay (p = 0.016) but not with mortality. No demographic factor predicted shorter LOS. Survival analysis showed no significant difference between inpatient mortality across hypokalaemia severity groups (moderate or severe) (p = 0.190). Faster correction of serum potassium was weakly associated with shorter LOS.

CONCLUSION: In this large cohort of hospitalised adults with moderate to severe hypokalaemia, cardiac telemetry was underutilised and not consistently applied according to the severity of electrolyte derangement. Instead, its use was more closely tied to patient comorbidities. Hypokalaemia severity alone was not an independent predictor of inpatient mortality or LOS. These findings support the need for standardised risk-stratified approaches to application of cardiac telemetry monitoring in hypokalaemia management, particularly in tertiary centres serving broad and remote populations.
